title: Graceful stream backpressure SDK shims with schema contracts and tool multiplexing
creator: Anya Caldwell
description: Goal: Ship a cross-language SDK shim layer that provides (1) graceful client-side backpressure controls for streaming token/JSONL outputs, (2) schema-driven progressive validation for structured outputs, and (3) an opt-in tool/function multiplexing contract so a single stream can carry model tokens, structured events, and tool invocation frames without breaking older clients. Rationale: Customers embedding streaming LLM responses need stable client semantics when we add structured events and tool calls into streaming. Existing language SDKs occasionally drop chunks or throw parse errors when interleaved JSON tool frames arrive mid-stream. This work minimizes breakage and gives clear migration paths.
acceptance_criteria: 1) TypeScript, Python, and Go SDKs expose a minimal 'StreamController' API that supports pause()/resume(), maxBufferedBytes, and onFrame hooks. 2) Progressive NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) schema validator runs on each structured frame and emits validation errors but continues streaming non-blocking. 3) Tool multiplexing frames follow a small envelope format: {type: 'token'|'event'|'tool', id: string, payload: <string|json>}. Older clients can ignore unknown types without failing. 4) Examples and migration guide published: TS/py/go snippets showing backpressure in low-memory environments, tool mux example, and graceful downgrade. 5) Integration tests for interleaved streams, and e2e perf tests showing <=5% median latency increase.
design_notes:
- Chose NDJSON progressive parsing because it's forgiving for partial chunks and easy to validate per-line.
- Backpressure: expose both token-count and byte-based limits; implement a ring buffer with soft-drop policy for low-priority informational events.
- Multiplexing envelope keeps payload opaque for simple token consumers; SDKs decode known 'event' and 'tool' types, and surface unknown types as 'opaque' frames.
- Compatibility layer: add a feature flag 'enableMuxedStream' on client side; server defaults to off for GA but will advertise capability via /models metadata.
- Avoid breaking change: streaming plain text still works as before; interleaving only occurs when both sides advertise the capability.
- Security: we validate schemas locally; any schema mismatch is recorded but not sent upstream as PII.
- Perf: parsing implemented with streaming parser (simd-json for Go, rapidjson/C bindings for TS via wasm optional) to reduce overhead.
implementation_plan: 1) Define StreamController interface and envelope spec (week 1). 2) Implement Node TS shim and example app (week 2). 3) Implement Python asyncio shim with backpressure-aware async iterator (week 2). 4) Implement Go reader/writer with context cancellation and byte-budgeting (week 3). 5) Add schema validator and per-line error hook across languages (week 3). 6) Integration tests + perf harness + docs (week 4).
migration_notes:
- Default behavior unchanged for existing clients.
- To opt into tool multiplexing, client sets header 'X-Redwood-Stream: multiplex=v1' or uses SDK flag enableMuxedStream=true.
- Provide a small shim library for older SDKs to run in 'compat' mode which strips event frames into trailing logs.
- Document common pitfalls: partial-line boundaries, mixed encodings, and avoiding blocking on schema validation.
examples: TypeScript example: const ctrl = Redwood.stream({model:'rwd-small', enableMuxedStream:true}); for await (const frame of ctrl) { if(frame.type==='token') process.stdout.write(frame.payload); else if(frame.type==='event' && frame.schema==='answer') handleAnswer(frame.payload); }

Python example: async for frame in stream_controller.stream(): if frame['type']=='token': sys.stdout.write(frame['payload']) elif frame['type']=='tool': await tool_dispatch(frame['id'], frame['payload'])

Go example: r := sdk.NewStreamReader(resp.Body); for { frame, err := r.Next() if err==io.EOF { break } switch frame.Type { case 'token': fmt.Print(frame.Payload) case 'tool': go dispatchTool(frame.ID, frame.Payload) } }
test_plan:
- Unit tests: parser boundary cases, schema validator errors, backpressure pause/resume semantics.
- Integration: server produces interleaved token/event/tool frames at various rates to assert client stays under memory budgets.
- E2E perf: compare baseline streaming plain text vs muxed stream in median and p95 latency using runtime perf harness.
- Compatibility test matrix: old-client vs new-server; new-client vs new-server; new-client vs old-server.
- Fuzzing: inject malformed envelope headers and ensure SDK doesn't crash.
